title: A search of TESS light curves (2018 to 2026) of 648 hot-Jupiter hosts finds a 1.8-Earth-radius planet candidate at 2.0 days near WASP-105 b and a V-shaped 0.81-day signal near HATS-70 b
abstract: We searched the TESS light curves of 666 confirmed transiting hot Jupiters for more periodic transits. We used one PDCSAP light curve per sector to sector 107 (2026), masked the hot-Jupiter transits, and ran a box search from 0.3 to 40 days with a new C kernel. 648 hosts had data (3,779 sectors), and 602 hosts have sectors 70 to 107 that an earlier uniform search did not use. Of 676 threshold-crossing events, automatic tests for gaps, red noise, sector consistency, variability, odd/even depths and duration left 4. Pixel-level tests then left one strong candidate. Near WASP-105 b, a 2.002808-day signal of 350 +- 30 ppm (about 1.8 Earth radii) occurs in 9 sectors. Its depths agree in three photometry products, and its centroid and per-pixel depth images agree with the on-target hot Jupiter. Its duration agrees with a central transit. Near HATS-70 b, a consistent 0.814264-day signal of about 800 ppm is V-shaped and lies in a crowded field, so a blended eclipsing binary is a strong alternative. Centroid tests put strong dips near WASP-24, TOI-3053 and OGLE-TR-113 on other stars. The search found 6 of 11 known companions blind, including WASP-132 c, WASP-47 e and TOI-4468 c. In 177 injection tests the pipeline recovered 71% of planets at 0.5 to 2 days and 15% at 10 to 40 days. The candidates are not confirmed and need imaging, ground photometry and radial velocities.
